title: Overview
heading: Follow the work
text: Follow the work A queue coordinates work; it does not turn an unclear request into a verified fix by itself. A finished provider session is evidence of execution, not proof of correctness. Review, verification, and delivery permissions remain separate decisions.

title: Overview
heading: What is available
text: What is available The browser includes project overview, issue sources, task management, Plan Studio, named queues, agent roles, activity, usage, providers, approvals, operations, knowledge, and settings. Task details include Ask ATL, relationships, evidence, and captured change review. The runtime adds CLI automation, isolated workspaces, recovery, history transport, research records, source navigation, backups, and a multi-project supervisor. Use the [feature map](guides.md) to find each procedure, implementing module, and verifier. Search indexes every public guide. Diagrams render locally without a CDN and remain readable as Mermaid source in Markdown. This documentation describes the October 29, 2026 source snapshot and package version 0.1.3. Screenshots use synthetic local data. See the [verification record](docs-refresh-verification.md) for checks and limits.

title: Getting started
heading: Prerequisites
text: Prerequisites Use Node.js 22 or newer and Git. Provider execution additionally needs a supported installed CLI or a configured API provider. Python is used by repository policy verifiers. Browser verification uses Playwright and its installed browser.

title: Getting started
heading: Install the runtime
text: Install the runtime On macOS or Linux, use sh scripts/install-atl.sh . Open a new terminal afterward and run atl --help . The installer creates a per-user runtime; each managed application keeps its own state. To develop ATL itself, use node runtime/atl-manager.mjs --help from the clone. Run npm ci for documentation and verification dependencies.

title: Getting started
heading: Install the skills
text: Install the skills Restart your agent session. Invoke $atl with the engineering problem; the router chooses the smallest applicable process. See the [skill catalog](skills.md).

title: Getting started
heading: Initialize the application
text: Initialize the application Open the loopback URL printed by ATL. atl control-plane opens the same browser interface. atl tui opens the terminal interface; atl dashboard --once --plain prints a snapshot. Check any ATL_PROJECT override before initializing or running commands. Expected result: the Control Plane shows the intended project. Initialization creates .trust/manager/ there. Opening the browser does not launch a worker.

title: Getting started
heading: Create one bounded task
text: Create one bounded task 1. Open Tasks to create work, or Issue sources to import it. 2. Review its objective, observable checks, risk, prerequisites, and resources. 3. Use Plan Studio when the request needs clarification or decomposition. 4. Inspect provider readiness in Settings . 5. Add approved work to a queue and preview its launch and budget. 6. Confirm the bounded run, then inspect evidence and independent review. Expected result: an explicit task packet and queue membership precede execution. A successful session still needs completion evidence.

title: Getting started
heading: Recover setup problems
text: Recover setup problems If atl is missing, open a new terminal or use the installer-created shim. If the port is occupied, choose another port. Fix provider installation/authentication before repeating preview. See [troubleshooting](troubleshooting.md) and [providers](providers.md).

title: Control Plane
heading: Open your project
text: Open your project Run from the managed application, open the printed 127.0.0.1 URL, and check the project name. See [getting started](getting-started.md) for installation and [interface reference](team-interfaces.md) for the complete menu map.

title: Control Plane
heading: Follow the owner workflow
text: Follow the owner workflow 1. Read Overview for blockers and pending decisions. 2. Use Issue sources , Tasks , or Plan Studio to describe work. 3. Inspect objectives, checks, prerequisites, routing, and resources. 4. Select a queue and inspect preview, budget, and blocked items. 5. Confirm execution and watch Activity & Logs . 6. Inspect task evidence, Review changes , and independent review. 7. Decide whether delivery is ready and authorize the intended action. A preview is information. Confirmation authorizes a particular operation. Queue membership, task approval, and remote publishing have different effects.

title: Issue sources
heading: Prerequisites
text: Prerequisites Open the managed project in the Control Plane. Have read access to the source and put credentials in the ATL server’s environment. The page stores token environment variable names, not their values. Use synthetic hosts and injected adapters for tests.

title: Issue sources
heading: Configure the connector
text: Configure the connector Open Issue sources , enter its fields, and save. Source Enter Authentication --- --- --- GitHub Repository names such as example/demo Authenticated gh CLI or GITHUB_TOKEN ; public repositories may allow anonymous reads Jira Base URL such as https://jira.example.invalid , project keys APP, OPS Token variable, default JIRA_TOKEN Azure Boards Organization/collection URL, project, optional iteration PAT variable, default AZDO_PAT For https://devops.example.invalid:32678/Collection/Project/_workitems/recentlyupdated/ , enter https://devops.example.invalid:32678/Collection as the organization URL and Project as the project. A sprint taskboard URL is a browser view, not the connector base. Enter the iteration separately, for example Project\Sprint 74 . Expected result: a settings-saved message. Saving does not import issues.

title: Issue sources
heading: Preview and import
text: Preview and import 1. Choose Preview for a configured source. 2. Search or filter candidates. 3. Select the intended issues and import them. 4. Inspect the reported queue, then open Tasks and Queues . 5. Check the imported source identity, revision, objective, and checks. ![Issue sources in a synthetic project](assets/screenshots/sources.jpg) Preview creates no tasks. Import creates local candidates with source identity and revision metadata. Deduplication is source-aware; avoid editing identities by hand.

title: Issue sources
heading: Plan description-only work
text: Plan description-only work Open the imported request in Plan Studio . Record constraints and questions, generate a repository-grounded plan, inspect proposals, and request separate review. Resolve findings before approving a new queue. A local template is a preview, not a provider-reviewed plan. A changed source revision invalidates approval evidence. Refresh and review against the current issue. See [Plan Studio](plan-studio.md) and its [contract](plan-studio-contract.md).

title: Issue sources
heading: Recover connector errors
text: Recover connector errors Check enablement, URL shape, selected repositories/projects, token availability in the server environment, and network access. Preserve the adapter error. Do not substitute a production issue for an offline fixture. Jira intake does not imply Jira writeback; plan publishing currently targets GitHub/Azure.

title: Issue sources

Run node verification/jira_adapter_contract_test.mjs , node verification/github_adapter_contract_test.mjs , node verification/azure_issue_journey_test.mjs , or node verification/issue_source_ui_journey_test.mjs from the clone. text: Plan Studio Use Plan Studio when a request describes an outcome but lacks independently executable tasks. Planning proposes work; review and owner approval decide whether it can enter an execution queue.

title: Plan Studio
heading: Prepare the request
text: Prepare the request Open Plan Studio with a request or imported issue. State the outcome, constraints, project, and acceptance examples. Distinguish observed evidence from assumptions. Start with [issue sources](issue-sources.md) for external work.

title: Plan Studio
heading: Generate and review
text: Generate and review 1. Inspect planning provider readiness and resource allowance. 2. Generate a plan and inspect requirements, evidence, assumptions, questions, risks, and task proposals. 3. Answer questions and correct objectives, deliverables, prerequisites, files, checks, and skill reasons. 4. Request separate provider review of the current artifact. 5. Resolve blocking findings and verify the source revision. 6. Approve the reviewed artifact to create an execution queue. ![Plan Studio in the synthetic documentation project](assets/screenshots/studio.jpg) Expected result: an approved plan creates bounded task packets in a queue. Editing after review invalidates its binding. A stale source revision blocks approval. A description or local preview is insufficient evidence.

title: Plan Studio
heading: Publish deliberately
text: Publish deliberately Inspect Publish destination , preview its GitHub or Azure destination, then confirm the exact publication. Local queue creation and remote issue creation are separate operations. Inspect existing publication mapping before retrying to avoid duplicates.

title: Plan Studio
heading: Resolve an approval block
text: Resolve an approval block Read validation findings. Missing answers, insufficient checks, stale sources, legacy artifacts, and unresolved review findings need an updated artifact and review. See the [plan contract](plan-studio-contract.md) for fields and bindings. Source: runtime/lib/plan-studio.mjs , plan-model.mjs , plan-publish.mjs . Checks: verification/plan_contract_test.mjs , plan_studio_journey_test.mjs , and plan_publish_test.mjs .

A useful check names behavior and a verifier: “Submitting an empty email displays validation and sends no request; run the form regression test.” “Fix the page” does not define acceptance.

title: Overnight runs
heading: An overnight run executes approved work within session, concurrency, and time limits. It needs a running machine, a ready provider, and execution authority. It cannot gua
text: Overnight runs An overnight run executes approved work within session, concurrency, and time limits. It needs a running machine, a ready provider, and execution authority. It cannot guarantee an error-free delivery from an arbitrary description.

title: Overnight runs
heading: Prepare and launch
text: Prepare and launch 1. Complete task contracts and reviewed plans, including prerequisite handoffs. 2. Select the queue and inspect resource policy and provider readiness. 3. Preview and read every blocker, model selection, and allowance. 4. Confirm the intended bounded run and watch its first session. These are example limits, not a promise of eight successful tasks. Other gates can constrain execution. See [resource policy](resource-policy.md).

title: Overnight runs
heading: Monitor, stop, and recover
text: Monitor, stop, and recover Follow Queues , Activity & Logs , and Usage & Limits . Use the exposed stop operation and inspect resulting state. Reconcile an existing run after a restart before launching again. Preserve failed commands, output, revisions, and blockers. Apply bounded repairs and rerun checks; do not reset counters to evade limits. See [queue recovery](queue-recovery.md) and [reliability](task-run-reliability.md).

title: Overnight runs
heading: Assess delivery
text: Assess delivery Inspect each task’s current-revision checks, independent review, diagnostics, captured changes, and delivery record. Verify prerequisite artifacts were consumed. Missing usage remains unknown. Task completion, a local delivery branch, a draft PR, a merged PR, and production deployment are distinct outcomes. Record the actual boundary reached. Remote actions need the corresponding permission and checks.

title: Overnight runs
heading: Reproduce the offline exercise
text: Reproduce the offline exercise Run node verification/run_mock_regression.mjs from the ATL clone. It records per-test evidence and aggregate results under .atl-evidence/mock-regression/ . The [recorded run](mock-system-e2e-2026-10-29.md) separates failures, accomplishments, and lessons. Fixture workers establish orchestration behavior; they do not prove real model quality or production delivery.

title: Ask ATL
heading: Ask about a task
text: Ask about a task 1. Open a task and choose Ask ATL , or open the project conversation from navigation. 2. Inspect the suggested focus and its evidence source. Use it as a starting hypothesis, not an established diagnosis. 3. Choose discussion or fix mode and inspect provider readiness and context. 4. Write the question. Use suggested question only fills the composer; it does not send. 5. Send deliberately. A fix needs approval of the exact request and usable workspace access. 6. Read the reply, inspect cited evidence, and retain the conversation. Completion still requires independent review and current checks. If access fails, follow the recovery procedure below. Saving access or checking it does not automatically retry a provider request. Ask ATL is available from a task's details or the project navigation. Each message has a Copy button; Copy conversation includes the stored messages. Copying preserves the original text and Markdown. Replies render paragraphs, lists, emphasis and code without allowing message HTML to execute. Ask ATL now opens with a suggested focus based on recorded task state. It prioritizes unmet prerequisites, failed current-revision checks, recovery issues, exhausted session allowances and blockers. The project conversation points to a blocked task first. Use suggested question fills the composer without sending or approving a provider run. The suggestion names its evidence source and is a hypothesis: the provider must check it against current logs, recovery records and workspace evidence. Older conversation turns are shortened in the provider prompt to leave room for current evidence; the saved transcript and Copy conversation remain complete. The composer stays below the scrolling conversation. New output follows the bottom until you scroll up. Jump to latest returns to new output. Provider activity and diagnostic disclosures retain their open state during polling. Drafts, provider choice and mode survive opening Workspace access and returning within the same page. Ctrl/Cmd+Enter requests sending; task fixes still use the existing exact-request approval and independent review gates. ![Ask ATL project conversation entry in the synthetic Control Plane](assets/screenshots/ask-atl.jpg)

title: Ask ATL
heading: Recover from an access failure
text: Recover from an access failure 1. In the conversation, choose Fix workspace access , or open Workspace access from the task's details. 2. Select Read, edit and run commands in the task workspace , then choose Apply task access . Select Use project default to remove an override. 3. Choose Check workspace access . On Windows this runs a local GapCode sandbox command which creates, reads and removes a unique temporary file in the task workspace. It uses no model session and no task-session budget. 4. Return to the conversation and choose Prepare retry . Inspect the message and use Send message to review the normal approval request. Saving access and checking access do not automatically retry the failed provider request. For a shared default, use Settings → Workspace access → Default workspace access → Save access default . This project setting applies to all models of the built-in GapCode and Codex CLI adapters, for Ask ATL and queue workers. Task overrides take precedence. Diagnose conversations remain read-only. Custom CLI adapters retain their own contracts; no machine-wide GapCode/Codex configuration is changed. Settings are stored in config/manager.json : Only read-only and workspace-write are accepted. An absent setting retains the existing workspace-write default. Changes affect future runs and preserve task budgets, evidence, repair allowances and independent review gates. Browser mutations require the same owner session and CSRF protection as other Control Plane operations.

title: Ask ATL
heading: What the check proves
text: What the check proves On Windows, GapCode now receives the named :workspace or :read-only permission profile and the existing unelevated Windows sandbox setting. Ask ATL previously passed only the legacy --sandbox workspace-write flag, unlike queue workers. Both launch paths now share one permission adapter; On Windows, both built-ins now receive the matching named permission profile: the codex executable may itself be GapCode's standalone alias. Non-Windows invocations keep the sandbox-mode flags. Before a real GapCode-backed fix, ATL runs a local read/write/remove sandbox probe before charging a model session. A failed probe returns its exact diagnostic. If a provider nevertheless starts read-only, ATL stops it immediately and preserves that failure category. The October 29 T-023 incident reproduced this distinction: its codex alias started read-only with only --sandbox workspace-write , and started writable with the matching default_permissions=":workspace" and Windows profile. The local sandbox read/write/remove check passed for that selected executable. Dependency readiness is separate. A task with dependencies needs its locked installation and matching .atl-dependencies.json receipt. Set workspaces.provisionLocal: true to authorize automatic offline npm ci with scripts disabled. The runtime uses its project-local npm cache and never downloads packages in that automatic route. If the cache is incomplete, it reports the exact npm error/package. A deliberate owner-authorized dependency installation can populate the cache; subsequent recovery verifies the receipt. Neither readiness nor unblocking proves an acceptance check or review passed. A successful local check proves sandbox filesystem access. It does not grant approval to external MCP tools, override managed policy, verify a model's commands, approve work or complete a task. If filesystem access passes but a model's MCP tool still needs approval, inspect that tool's configuration and approval mechanism. The interface distinguishes this tool-policy failure from a provider account/model error. A zero exit with denied access is a failed fix, rather than work ready for review.

title: Ask ATL
heading: Browser tools for rendered checks
text: Browser tools for rendered checks October 29, 2026 working-tree runtime: tasks whose objective, checks or skills require rendered inspection receive the atl_browser MCP server in Rowan, Sage and Beacon sessions. An integrated Beacon delivery also receives it. Task-scoped Ask ATL Fix uses the same tools. Diagnose remains read-only and does not start a browser. The built-in GapCode, Codex and Claude queue adapters attach session-local MCP configuration. Custom provider commands remain responsible for their own browser tooling; the runtime does not inject an incompatible MCP configuration into them or waive their evidence gates. No user-level provider configuration or approval policy is changed. If the host rejects a call because its approval policy is never , use Task details → Browser access → Allow ATL test browser → Apply browser access . This authorizes the seven isolated preview tools for that task's future GapCode/Codex runs. The failure panel's Fix browser access button opens this control directly. Saving never starts a model run or unblocks the task automatically; review and send the next request separately. For a shared default, use Settings → Browser access → Save browser default . Each task can Use project default , Require approval , or Allow ATL test browser . A task restriction takes precedence over an allowed project default. Check browser runtime starts and closes a disposable test browser without spending a model session or task budget. It verifies the runtime, not effective model-tool approval. Host-managed restrictions still take precedence; the Claude adapter retains its own permission handling. The UI stores only this isolated-browser policy in config/manager.json : Choosing Use project default removes the task override. The legacy ui_review.local_browser_tools_approved flag remains a fallback when no UI default is saved. Other MCP tools, browser profiles and live task mutations retain their permissions. Browser changes require the existing owner session and CSRF protection. Task budgets, recovery history and evidence are preserved. Restart an older Control Plane server after updating its runtime. The model starts browser_preview , reads browser_snapshot , interacts with browser_action , reads computed directions and isolation with browser_inspect , and calls browser_screenshot . The screenshot is returned as an image to the model and saved with UTF-8 DOM/style observations, viewport, locale, timestamps, asset hashes and a screenshot hash under the task's .atl-evidence/ui-review/ . browser_viewport supports mobile checks and browser_reload refreshes repaired assets. Preview starts an isolated Playwright browser with disposable Control Plane fixture state; it does not use the user's Chrome profile or expose live manager mutations. Navigation and browser requests are restricted to the fixture origin and GET/HEAD. This initial adapter covers ATL Control Plane assets, not arbitrary websites. Playwright must resolve from the project or task workspace. ATL prefers its installed Chromium; ATL_BROWSER_EXECUTABLE can select an existing browser binary. Missing dependencies are reported before a worker session starts; an executable path alone does not establish a working browser connection. browser_preview establishes that connection. A host denial remains an environment blocker, not permission to relax policy or claim a PASS. Capture receipts deliberately say NOT OBSERVED . The model must examine the image, compare the requested behavior, and submit its exact check and current source revision through the existing scoped observe command. Capturing an image never completes a task or replaces independent review. A local T-022 rendering check can precede T-024's integrated review. Regression verification: node verification/ui_review_mcp_test.mjs exercises the actual stdio handshake, provider argument injection, browser startup, Persian fixture, image return, evidence artifacts and shutdown. It verifies tool transport, not a model's visual judgment or T-022 completion. An October 29 real Ask ATL smoke session without browser authorization was denied by the host's never policy. A second isolated smoke project enabled only its task's browser permission. GapCode / gpt-6-luna then called preview, snapshot, action, inspection and screenshot tools; received and inspected the returned image; and reported the Persian sentence as RTL with its Latin path LTR and isolated. The transcript and screenshot are under .trust/browser-tool-smoke-1793253400838/ . This proves the model-to-browser path in that environment. It does not complete T-022 or replace its review; the live project's permissions and task state were not changed. verification/browser_access_test.mjs verifies project/task inheritance, the exact per-tool provider arguments, owner/CSRF enforcement, snapshots, legacy compatibility and preserved budgets/state. The desktop/mobile path through task settings, project defaults and the failure shortcut is covered by verification/control_plane_modal_test.mjs . These checks are included in the runtime CI workflow; remote CI has not been observed for this change.

title: Ask ATL
heading: October 28, 2026 observation
text: October 28, 2026 observation T-022's saved failed fix used gapgpt / gpt-6-luna . Its diagnostic reported command-policy denials and an MCP call requiring approval while the nested session's approval policy was never . The earlier instruction to choose a different provider conflated filesystem access with tool execution policy. After unifying the profile arguments, a real GapCode sandbox check inside T-022's workspace passed read/write/readback/cleanup. No additional model run or task session was used. A model-driven repair and independent T-022 review remain separate, unobserved gates for this change. This does not restore consumed sessions or erase failure history. Use the current project server for these endpoints; restart an older Control Plane server after updating its runtime.

title: Review changes
heading: Open a task in the live browser Control Plane and select Review changes. Diagram opens the Relationships tab. Inspection does not start workers, change task status, or gr
text: Reviewing task changes Open a task in the live browser Control Plane and select Review changes . Diagram opens the Relationships tab. Inspection does not start workers, change task status, or grant delivery approval.

title: Review changes
heading: Operator workflow
text: Operator workflow 1. Read the status and attention items on Overview. Blocked tasks remain blocked even when checks passed. Title, objective, and latest summary come from task records. 2. Check the baseline/output content identifiers and capture time. These are SHA-256 source revisions, not Git commits. The revision selector opens earlier captures. Refresh evidence keeps the selected source pinned. 3. Open Files. Expand directories, search loaded paths, or filter by change type. Select a file to load its diff. Use Load more files to include later pages in search/filtering. Patches load individually. 4. Open Evidence. current means both packet and code revision match; result and coverage remain separate. Revisionless evidence is unknown ; old and invalidated evidence stay visibly labeled. Task-level evidence is not automatically proof for one file. 5. Open Relationships to inspect actual task, change-set, snapshot, file, evidence and artifact-reference data. File records open diffs; evidence records open observations. Artifact hashes are references only, without a content-availability claim. Run links and structured decisions are explicitly unavailable when not established by source records. Completed handoffs can be inspected after their workspace is archived. Active or blocked work needs Capture current changes . Capture stores immutable inspection data and compares two successive snapshots; a mismatch prevents publication. It never invents a missing baseline from Git HEAD. Pause a busy worker before capturing if consistency errors persist.

title: Review changes
heading: Model and trust boundary
text: Model and trust boundary Record Contract --- --- Change set Version 1, deterministic ID from task + packet + baseline + output, task ID, packet revision, capture time, source kind, nullable run ID and imported input revisions. Snapshot Existing {revision, files, modes} identity; retain source bytes/hashes. File change Path-derived ID, relative path, kind, before/after hashes and modes. Add/modify/delete/mode-only changes are supported; rename inference is deferred. Evidence Existing observation plus stable inspection reference and freshness. Matching requires explicit packet/code revisions. Artifact Observation hash and evidence/revision pointers; reference_only does not prove the artifact is available. Directory Derived grouping of loaded paths, not a separate ownership record. Attention Deterministic blocker, missing verification/review, stale evidence or failed/incomplete observation flags. No generated assurance score. state.json owns lifecycle/evidence; handoffs.mjs owns verified handoffs. Inspection artifacts cannot satisfy completion checks or approvals. Context knowledge stays advisory. Comparing captured baseline to output excludes pre-existing dirty files unchanged by the worker. Imported predecessor revisions remain visible; a composed diff is not an authorship claim.

title: Review changes
heading: Storage and API
text: Storage and API Captures publish .trust/manager/change-reviews/ / .json and reuse .trust/manager/handoffs/blobs/ . Blobs precede manifest publication. A same-volume hard link publishes manifests without replacing a concurrent capture with the same ID; partial temporary files are ignored. Completed handoffs use the existing validator. A bounded cache reuses validated handoffs while identity/file metadata stay unchanged; requested blob previews always verify hashes again. Endpoint Purpose --- --- GET /api/task-changes?taskId=...&changeSetId=...&cursor=...&limit=... Pinned/latest metadata, history, evidence and attention; does not create captures. GET /api/task-change-diff?taskId=...&changeSetId=...&fileId=... Bounded preview for a file belonging to that task/change set. POST /api/task-changes/capture Explicit capture; JSON { "task_id": "T-001" } . All three require the owner cookie and x-atl-csrf header, including source-reading GET requests. Capture also uses the existing origin checks. The browser never supplies arbitrary filesystem paths. Periodic snapshots/SSE contain no patches or new capture work. Paths reject traversal, symlinks and Windows junctions. Record associations, manifest hashes and requested blob hashes are checked.

title: Review changes
heading: Bounds and missing data
text: Bounds and missing data - Metadata returns at most 100 file rows/page. Aggregate line totals stay unknown; loading one diff computes its counts. No complete-review badge is inferred. - Text allows 1 MiB/side, 20,000 lines/side and 256 KiB patch output. Line comparison caps its LCS matrix at 2,000,000 cells with a five-second computation budget. Limits/timeouts are explicit states; binary/non-UTF-8 content is labeled binary. - Capture preflight caps source at 10,000 files, 32 MiB/file and 128 MiB total. Git enumeration has a five-second limit. A capture taking over ten seconds does not publish an inspection manifest. These are synchronous local captures; large workspaces can briefly occupy the server. No automatic captures are enabled. - .env , credential/secret files, private-key containers and common token assignments suppress the whole preview as redacted . This conservative filter is not a guarantee that every secret is detected. Source blobs retain original bytes; keep sensitive content out of task workspaces under existing workspace policy. - Missing baseline returns baseline_missing , uncaptured work capture_required . Missing workspaces/blobs and corruption stay explicit. A corrupt newest record is not silently displayed as empty changes. Earlier explicit captures remain independent of task packet changes. - Two filesystem observations cannot prove transactional consistency or detect a change-and-revert between them. Capture checks the task's packet/baseline/workspace/input contract again before publication. It does not lock an active worker. - Existing global shortcuts are suspended inside the dialog. Tabs, directory controls and focus cycling use native controls; code/paths remain isolated LTR in Persian layouts. - No scheduled digest, automatic retention cleanup or shared-blob deletion is introduced. Structured decision capture and semantic dependency analysis remain follow-up work.

title: Review changes
heading: Verification and rollback
text: Verification and rollback The UI suite exercises async controller state and escaped markup in a DOM double. It does not prove browser layout, native keyboard behavior, responsive rendering or accessibility. For rendered checks, run node verification/fixtures/task-changes/serve.mjs and open its printed URL through the supported browser integration. Its 115 changed files exercise pagination without using live manager state. Check dark/light themes, narrow width, keyboard navigation, refresh retention and Persian paths; stop the fixture process afterward. Validation on 2026-10-27: focused suites and existing dependency, queue recovery/delivery, Control Plane server/contract, run-control and CSS checks passed. Initial metadata generation for 1,000 paths measured 75.8 ms locally on Windows; this is not a production guarantee. Rendered verification remains OPEN: Chrome integration could not connect, and diagnostics reported missing extension/native-host setup. The Persian browser suite remains unrun for that reason. No visual or accessibility pass is claimed. The live server loads the additive ATL_CHANGE_REVIEW UI capability. Rollback removes its script injection/action and three routes, retaining inspection artifacts. Execution and delivery gates do not depend on this new store. The optional morning digest is deferred.

title: Queue recovery
heading: ATL prepares prerequisite outputs inside each worker's isolated workspace before starting a provider. Mira owns recovery, Pip owns one bounded contract repair, Rowan owns
text: Queue preparation, recovery, and delivery ATL prepares prerequisite outputs inside each worker's isolated workspace before starting a provider. Mira owns recovery, Pip owns one bounded contract repair, Rowan owns overlapping edits, Sage owns review, and Beacon owns verification. Existing work remains in place.

title: Queue recovery
heading: Prepare an executable task contract
text: Prepare an executable task contract Plan Studio proposals accept check_owners (completion check to proposal ID) and a dispatch_contract . Approval rejects prerequisite cycles, unknown prerequisites, and checks owned by downstream stages. The final plan card also verifies the composed output and all predecessor checks; it depends on every preceding card. Commands are argument arrays executed without a shell. They check readiness before a paid session; acceptance checks still belong to the later review and verification stages. The executable example above is a contract shape: supply your project's actual artifact names and command. For npm projects, a lockfile is required when dependencies exist. Set workspaces.provisionLocal to true in config/manager.json to permit runtime provisioning with npm ci --offline --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund . The cache remains under .trust/manager/npm-cache . Missing cached packages are reported as owner capabilities; recovery does not enable a network, run lifecycle scripts, or request credentials. A changed manifest or lockfile invalidates the preparation receipt. Other package managers and submodule handoffs require an explicit supported capability.

title: Queue recovery
heading: Inspect verified handoffs and waiting work
text: Inspect verified handoffs and waiting work The task detail's Review recovery action inventories the transitive prerequisite chain, recorded checks, evidence counts, available workspaces, and their changed files without altering them. Legacy completed tasks with no baseline are not automatically converted into verified handoffs: their output must be revalidated with trustworthy evidence. Dispatch previews report unverified prerequisite handoffs before a worker starts. Ask ATL , available from task details and the project navigation, starts an approval-gated provider session. Diagnose mode is read-only; task-scoped fix mode permits edits and checks within the existing task workspace and holds the queue run lock until the provider stops. Task sessions include the task brief, recent evidence, recovery status, and prerequisite handoff inventory; project sessions have project context. Messages and output are stored locally and are replayed as context for subsequent messages, rather than as a native persistent provider session. A successful fix session is marked awaiting review, not approved or verified. Review and run any resulting change separately through ATL's normal controls. Do not enter secrets in assistant messages. Task conversations receive the current packet revision, remaining session allowance, readiness contract, five recent recovery records (including failed preflights), and evidence invalidation markers. Project conversations receive up to 40 active tasks and their waiting reasons. The assistant is instructed to classify the failure, inspect evidence, avoid unchanged retries, and identify the exact owner decision when necessary. This context improves diagnosis; it does not grant authority or prove that a provider chose the correct repair. Version 1 records live under .trust/manager/handoffs/ . Each completed task records its baseline, content revision, file modes, changed files, SHA-256 blob hashes, input revisions, packet revision, and current complete check evidence. The state record also stores the manifest hash. Consumers verify the manifests and blobs before applying outputs. Dirty and untracked source can be handed off without committing the worker's checkout. Preparation journals make replay idempotent after interruption. Ancestor outputs are composed in prerequisite order. A reused workspace receives missing outputs while its existing edits remain intact. Conflicts are staged under its own .atl-inputs/ directory, including each predecessor's manifest and files. Rowan receives at most two integration sessions within the task's existing session allowance, followed by review and verification. queueInspect and the task detail view expose input revisions, the exact waiting reason, recovery owner, current repair action, and remaining attempts. Task state stores versioned recovery_records and its current recovery projection. Each record contains cause, evidence, attempted actions, their preflight outcomes, and escalation state.

title: Queue recovery
heading: Recover within the approved allowance
text: Recover within the approved allowance Each blocker permits at most two distinct remedies. A retry requires a successful preflight after a recorded repair. Repeating a failure after a successful repair escalates it; restarting the process or revising a packet does not restore consumed repair or session allowances. A restart during a local repair observes its postcondition before considering another action. Mira may request one Pip session for a discovered contract or verifier conflict. Its runtime request and resulting pip_repair record identify the approved objective, evidence, and packet revision. Pip writes a JSON packet inside its workspace and uses: The packet has patch and evidence fields. Patches may change prerequisites, readiness metadata, and check ownership. They cannot change the objective or completion checks, remove prerequisite artifacts or all existing readiness commands, create a cycle, or introduce downstream ownership. Evidence affected by the revision is retained and invalidated, including dependent task evidence. Pip does not receive a fresh session allowance. Waiting tasks are reevaluated after completions and successful repairs. Independent eligible work continues. Pending task IDs and run phases are persisted separately from result history. The supervisor can resume preparation, handoff, and local repair boundaries; an interrupted provider session remains owner-blocked until inspected. Run outcomes distinguish completed , waiting , exhausted , and owner-blocked , alongside operator abort and pause states. A task's done flag alone does not deliver its queue. A queue without an integrated delivery stage remains waiting for that stage and browser evidence.

title: Queue recovery
heading: Supervisor continuation and scheduled records
text: Supervisor continuation and scheduled records The supervisor lets the launch engine perform each task's bounded lifecycle and recovery. After a launch returns or throws, it moves to other eligible work instead of launching that same task repeatedly during the supervisor invocation. Subsequent launches receive only the remaining overall time allowance. Backup and scheduler failures are reported through the progress log. Routine ticks persist newly created runs and scheduler metadata together. Preview records do not consume execution eligibility. Cron occurrences remain distinct when the source fingerprint is unchanged; repeated ticks within the same occurrence deduplicate. Invalid schedules are recorded without preventing valid neighboring routines from being queued. Disabled routines do not retry, and unreadable or corrupt run storage raises an error instead of being replaced with empty state. These changes do not connect routine records to worker dispatch or keep an idle supervisor alive. Continuous overnight operation still requires that integration, host restart checks, and bounded live-provider trials. A queue settles as completed only with its existing delivery evidence; owner-blocked and exhausted work remains visible.

title: Queue recovery
heading: Deliver the composed revision
text: Deliver the composed revision Use atl revision T-002 to obtain the current content revision. Record observation packets under .atl-evidence/ , which is excluded from source snapshots, then submit them through atl observe T-002 .atl-evidence/check.json --actor beacon . A complete check packet includes: Sage records an approved review ; Beacon records a complete passing browser-journey . All predecessor checks, independent review, and the integrated browser journey must refer to the same composed content revision and current packet revision. Partial observations cannot pass an entire check. Only then does the runtime create atl/delivery- - with a separate Git index and record the integrated result in the existing delivery-packets.json store. It preserves the active branch and index and does not overwrite an existing delivery branch. No automatic main-branch merge, remote push, PR publication, or deployment follows.

title: Queue recovery
heading: Verify the recovery contract
text: Verify the recovery contract A worker's zero exit code does not prove progress. Newly recorded failed checks or unresolved review findings produce a verification-required blocker instead of another generic input-preparation retry. Its stable identity preserves repair accounting as diagnostic wording changes. Ask ATL presents the recorded causes, owners and next actions, and receives bounded worker-log tails. Approved fixes consume the existing task-session allowance; they cannot reset repair attempts or grant review approval. See [task-run reliability](task-run-reliability.md) for the isolated preview and [T-022's blocker ledger](../problems/enhancements/t022-ask-atl-recovery.md) for observed failure modes and remaining gates. The deterministic local provider fixture uses real child processes, isolated Git workspaces, offline npm provisioning, a real browser journey, and a local delivery branch. It exercises stale downstream input, a missing catalog, unavailable package network, discovered ownership conflicts, changed verifier assumptions, overlapping client edits, manifest corruption, restart replay, exhausted repair budgets, and owner-only blockers. It does not call a paid provider. Source of truth: runtime/lib/handoffs.mjs , dispatch-preflight.mjs , queue-recovery.mjs , launch.mjs , supervisor-runner.mjs , and delivery.mjs . Verified against this working-tree implementation by the regression command above; no release or remote revision is asserted.

title: Run reliability
heading: Observed 2026-10-27. Audience: maintainers operating task runs. Sources: T-022 worker transcripts and recovery records in .trust/manager/overnight/T-022/, the task feed,
text: Recurring task blockers: causes and prevention Observed 2026-10-27. Audience: maintainers operating task runs. Sources: T-022 worker transcripts and recovery records in .trust/manager/overnight/T-022/ , the task feed, the runtime implementation and executable verification suites.

title: Run reliability
heading: Why repeated retries failed
text: Why repeated retries failed The worker could edit its isolated workspace but attempted to persist its handoff in protected shared manager state and evidence storage. The sandbox correctly refused that write. Implementation checks could pass while the task remained in_progress . The runner treated the unchanged status as a stalled worker, retried preparation and spent sessions without changing the missing write mechanism. A separate credential failure affected direct launches that had no live lease. Recognizing either error prevents wasted retries but does not itself deliver a handoff. The repaired path is: worker writes a scoped request inside its workspace; manager authenticates the request against its task, role and live lease; manager invokes the existing gated command; manager saves shared state and evidence; worker receives the result. Worker sessions receive the local client, not the manager mutation credential. Evidence packets remain under .atl-evidence/ . Direct and queue launches both acquire and release leases. Credential lifetime covers the bounded worker session.

title: Run reliability
heading: Other observed failure chains
text: Other observed failure chains Cause How it becomes a blocker Repair and prevention --- --- --- Overlapping upstream files Integration dropped prior queue controls and plan context; reviewing only the small bidi patch missed the loss. Compare each conflicting predecessor snapshot, restore prior behavior, run consumer regressions, require independent review of the composed output. Hidden integration attempt cap Two prior attempts could prevent a repaired task from launching despite unused visible task budget. Use the persistent task session budget and count integration when the worker session starts. Preserve prior usage. Installed API paired with newer project UI Recovery button requested a route absent from the running installed server and displayed not found . ui-refresh imports matching project server and assets together. Running older processes must be restarted with the repaired runtime. Unscoped or stale worker credentials Direct launches lacked a lease; a worker could not submit its role handoff. Manager retains scoped credentials, validates lease generation for every command and releases the lease on exit. Incomplete bidi coverage Helper tests passed while queue log consumers still used plain escaping. Exercise actual consumers and review dynamic logs, evidence, paths and timestamp cells; retain fresh rendered evidence for the current source revision. These are observed failure classes, not a claim that every historical blocker had the same cause. No retry can manufacture provider access, human approval or an unavailable browser connection.

title: Run reliability
heading: Prevention during every task run
text: Prevention during every task run 1. Validate prerequisites, workspace and allowed commands before spending a worker session. Load the same runtime version for server and UI. 2. Establish a live lease and the workspace-local handoff channel. Keep manager state writes in the manager and evidence production in the worker workspace. 3. Reject cross-task, impersonated, expired and stale requests. Do not blindly replay an uncertain mutation after a timeout or channel shutdown. 4. Compose overlapping inputs explicitly. Preserve upstream behavior and run checks against the composed output, not just an isolated patch. 5. Obtain independent review, rerun completion checks and publish a verified handoff for the current content revision. Never clear a gate merely to make the UI appear successful. 6. On failure, retain exact output and classify the cause. Retry only after a demonstrated repair or changed evidence; retain visible session accounting.

title: Run reliability
heading: Executable evidence
text: Executable evidence - verification/worker_channel_test.mjs : real filesystem sandbox denies direct shared-state writes while the client completes builder, review and verifier transitions; cross-task, actor impersonation, escaped packet paths, expired credentials, stale leases and closed channels fail. - verification/worker_channel_launch_test.mjs : actual spawned workers complete direct and queue runs through sandboxed clients and release leases. - verification/queue_recovery_delivery_test.mjs : stale workspace, missing catalog, overlapping inputs, predecessor preservation and verified delivery. - verification/overnight_recovery_test.mjs : restart boundaries and interruption recovery without silently reusing prior confirmation. - verification/ui_refresh_runtime_test.mjs : the CLI loads matching project server code instead of pairing newer assets with installed API routes. The handoff and UI-refresh regressions are included in the runtime CI matrix for Windows and Linux. T-022's later October 28 recovery is recorded in [the blocker ledger](../problems/enhancements/t022-ask-atl-recovery.md). Fresh CSS and real Chrome observations now satisfy its two completion checks at the current revision. Independent review and final completion remain pending; the task remains blocked and its session usage is still 12/23.

title: Run reliability
heading: Diagnose a worker that exits without advancing
text: Diagnose a worker that exits without advancing Ask ATL includes the current recovery plan, neighboring contracts, recent check/review evidence and two bounded, redacted worker-log tails. Each issue has an owner and next action. Fix mode consumes one remaining task session and preserves exhausted repair history. Its output still needs independent review; a successful assistant process does not approve or complete a task. When a worker records a failed verification or unresolved review and exits without advancing, the runner records that cause. Generic execution failures cannot use prepare-verified-inputs as proof of repair. The latest valid evidence for the current packet controls check and review gates, so an older pass cannot hide a later failure. Pip repair instructions apply only to Pip; workers cannot impersonate another role to rewrite acceptance ownership. For task-local rendered evidence, run the current project's helper with the task workspace as its argument: Open its loopback URL using the connected browser. It serves the task's assets with disposable UTF-8 fixture state under .atl-evidence/ui-preview , rejects mutating HTTP requests, and does not copy live manager state. Inspect the required surface and record DOM observations and screenshots against the task revision. Creating the fixture alone does not pass a check, and this preview does not replace downstream integrated review. Passing these checks establishes the repaired paths. It cannot guarantee that all future providers, machines or task implementations will never fail. Ask ATL now provides task access controls, a project default for all built-in GapCode/Codex models, and a local sandbox access check that does not use a task session. See [Ask ATL conversations and workspace access](ask-atl.md) for the recovery steps, permission scope and observed limits.

title: Plan contract
heading: Follow Plan Studio to generate, clarify, review, and approve a plan. Inspect the current artifact, source revision, and review binding before approval. If validation fail
text: Plan Studio contract

title: Plan contract
heading: Apply the contract
text: Apply the contract Follow [Plan Studio](plan-studio.md) to generate, clarify, review, and approve a plan. Inspect the current artifact, source revision, and review binding before approval. If validation fails, update the artifact and obtain a fresh review rather than retrying stale evidence. Plan Contract v2 separates requirements, constraints, observed evidence, assumptions, open questions, acceptance examples, and risks. Every task links to requirements and records instructions, deliverables, prerequisites, affected paths, completion checks, a verifier, and a reason for each selected skill. Generated plans remain proposals. Approval requires a separate provider review with no unresolved consequential questions or major/blocker findings. The review is tied to the plan, original intent, and fingerprints of referenced files; editing a task or changing captured evidence clears its readiness. Local templates and legacy drafts remain useful for editing but cannot be approved as reviewed implementation plans. “Passed” means the artifact met its declared structure and the configured reviewer found no blocking issue. It is not a guarantee of correctness, a claim that checks ran, or authorization to execute work. GitHub, Jira, and Azure intake records preserve the remote identity and revision as source context when a task is sent to Plan Studio. Imported work is blocked from execution until its source task receives an approved Plan Studio accuracy review. The publish preview shows create or update actions; publishing requires a fresh review and explicit confirmation. Existing remote records are checked against their last recorded revision, and successful mappings are saved after each item so a retry does not create duplicates. GitHub publishing uses GITHUB_TOKEN ; Azure uses the configured intake.azure project and its token_env (default AZDO_PAT ).

title: Providers and access
heading: Choose a ready provider and an eligible model before execution. Authentication, model capability, workspace access, and browser access are separate launch inputs.
text: Providers and access Choose a ready provider and an eligible model before execution. Authentication, model capability, workspace access, and browser access are separate launch inputs.

title: Providers and access
heading: Configure a provider
text: Configure a provider Open Settings and inspect built-in readiness. Install and authenticate the chosen CLI, or configure an API provider with its base URL, protocol, credential, and models. A supported CLI subscription and an API key are different authentication paths. Inspect [CLI reference](cli-reference.md) before changing provider keys or overrides. Keep credentials out of task descriptions, screenshots, and research records.

title: Providers and access
heading: Validate model selection
text: Validate model selection Configure resource-policy model tiers and relative cost order. Inspect the effective task provider/model and role overrides in launch preview. A cheaper incapable tier must be rejected before spend. Cost order is a local ordering, not a currency estimate. Execution reports identify the configured model; undocumented provider substitutions remain unknown. See [model routing](model-routing.md) and [resource policy](resource-policy.md).

title: Providers and access
heading: Review execution and browser access
text: Review execution and browser access Use Settings to inspect access mode and readiness probes before a task needs files or a rendered UI. Discussing a task in Ask ATL does not grant a fix request access. Saving access settings does not prove completion.

title: Providers and access
heading: Recover authentication or quota errors
text: Recover authentication or quota errors Preserve provider errors and quota evidence. Unknown remote capacity remains unknown. Before fallback, inspect whether the alternative is permitted, ready, and capable. Re-run preview after fixing configuration. Checks: verification/execution_access_test.mjs , browser_access_test.mjs , provider_quota_failover_test.mjs .

title: Resource policy
heading: Settings → Autonomous resources controls the project-local resource_policy in config/manager.json. Save does not start a provider or queue. Existing projects retain their
text: Adaptive task resources Settings → Autonomous resources controls the project-local resource_policy in config/manager.json . Save does not start a provider or queue. Existing projects retain their old behavior until the policy is enabled. Policy changes wait for an active queue to finish; restarting a server is not a way to change the allowance of an already running session. The default session count is editable independently of automatic estimation. With adaptive budgets enabled, the initial estimate is 3 sessions for a small routine task, the configured default for standard work, default + 4 for complex work, and default + 8 for critical work. A review rejection adds room for repair. The run allowance, overall time limit, and automatic per-task ceiling still apply. Estimates count all lifecycle roles, including review and verification. Unused sessions are an allowance, not work ATL must perform. Only allocations marked source: automatic may grow automatically. With automatic extension enabled, the manager can reserve the remaining lifecycle handoffs at each session boundary, up to the ceiling. It never resets used . Legacy task limits and owner increases are pinned; changing a Settings default does not override them. An explicit run session limit can impose a lower cap. When extension is disabled, the first automatic allocation remains fixed. Model routing uses an owner-approved pool of exact provider/model pairs. Each pair has an economy, standard, or advanced capability tier, an enabled flag, and a cost order from 0 to 100. Cost order is a relative owner preference, not a price quotation. The strongest allowed tier and enabled rows together define the ceiling. Adding a provider connection does not automatically enroll its models. Installed model metadata supplies input suggestions; availability in a local catalog is not a guarantee of account entitlement or runtime success. Before each role session, ATL estimates required capacity from the task's own scope, files, dependencies, risk, acceptance surfaces and review results. A planner can supply a reasoned resource_estimate ; it cannot downgrade observed risk, choose an unauthorized provider, or increase a ceiling. Genuine review rejections increase required reasoning capacity; risky independent reviews use the advanced tier. The lowest configured cost order among available models meeting the requirement wins. This is an inspectable bounded routing rule, not a learned price or performance predictor. Completed and independently verified execution histories now calibrate future session estimates and model tier requirements within the same owner bounds. See [Execution reports](execution-reports.md) for coverage, cohort thresholds and the distinction between runtime adaptation and model weight training. Explicit role or run selections are preserved and validated against the same pool, capacity requirement and ceiling. An unavailable or inadequate route stops before starting or charging a model session and names what is missing. No automatic fallback can cross the configured ceiling. Authentication, workspace/browser permissions, separate review and exact evidence gates remain independent requirements. Quota failover is enabled by default, independently of adaptive budgeting. When a CLI reports exhausted quota or a rate limit, ATL remembers a cooldown in .trust/manager/provider-quota.json , selects another eligible configured route, and continues the same lifecycle under the remaining session/time allowance. A failed attempt still consumes its session and appears in reports. An explicit role/model preference can be replaced for this quota recovery; turn off quota failover in Settings to prevent automatic retries. With a configured model pool, alternatives must meet the required capability and model ceiling. Without a pool and with automatic model routing off, ATL can use only existing configured provider defaults. It does not enroll a new provider or guess new model ids. Fresh verified quota observations are preferred over unknown alternatives. Unknown quota may be tried, but is never labelled available. A provider-wide failure skips that provider across tasks; a known model-scoped failure skips only that model. Quota cooldown defaults to thirty minutes; recognized rate limits use sixty seconds. No permanent lockout is inferred when a reset time is unavailable. If every eligible alternative is unavailable, the task retains its exact blocker and cooldown time; it cannot run through a quota, permission, model ceiling or budget boundary. Check: node verification/provider_quota_failover_test.mjs exercises a real two-task queue with an exhausted deterministic adapter and a working backup. Plan Studio shows a resource estimate for each task card and its build, review and verification roles. Its automatic provider option also applies the pool to generation, regeneration and plan accuracy review; each call keeps the existing one-session confirmation and timeout. Built-in subscription planning uses read-only permissions. Task details and launch preview show the decision; activity records resource_budget , resource_route and resource_route_blocked . Verification: node verification/resource_policy_test.mjs , node verification/resource_policy_ui_test.mjs , existing provider/Plan Studio and launch regression suites, and npm run ui:css:check .

title: Resource policy
heading: Per-task provider and model
text: Per-task provider and model Open a task, choose Actions → Provider / model , and select a configured provider and exact model. The choice is saved on that task and used for later Rowan, Sage, and Beacon sessions. Use project / automatic route removes the task choice. A provider/model explicitly selected for a particular run takes precedence over the saved task route. Changes are refused while a queue run is active, so an in-flight session keeps its original route. The resource policy's approved model pool and capability ceiling still apply.

title: Model routing
heading: ATL treats model choice as an engineering policy, not a prestige ranking. Route by the work:
text: Model routing and review ATL treats model choice as an engineering policy, not a prestige ranking. Route by the work: The default digital team has friendly names as well as explicit responsibilities: Mira coordinates, Pip triages, Rowan builds, Sage reviews, and Beacon verifies and keeps watch. Names are configurable; the role contract is what matters. Work Preferred role Required handoff --- --- --- implementation, refactor, debugging code plan, changed files, checks architecture, ambiguity, tradeoffs judgment decision, alternatives, risks reading, comparison, synthesis analysis cited findings and open questions SEO, metadata, and factual site copy content source-backed copy and acceptance evidence exploration and alternatives ideas candidate approaches and constraints The policy lives in [ config/model-routing.json ](../config/model-routing.json). Replace configure-me with models the team actually has access to, then run: The default loop is: The reviewer should use a different model or an intentionally independent context. If that is impossible, disclose it in the evidence packet and do not treat the result as an independent review. The default orchestration is deliberately conservative: one worker, then one independent review. Parallel workers are capped at three and are allowed only when their write sets are disjoint. Repair cycles are capped at two before escalation. These limits live in the orchestration section of the policy. Keep run records in .trust/agent-runs/ using the template there. Record exact model/version, tools, rationale, evidence links, outcome, and what should change in the playbook next time.

title: Model routing

title: Execution reports
heading: Inspect a report
text: Inspect a report 1. Open a task or queue and inspect Execution & resources and its session history. 2. Read provider/model, stage, allowance, retry, and quota-switch records together. 3. Compare token totals with session coverage; unknown usage is not zero. 4. Inspect current checks and independent review before reusing the result as calibration evidence. 5. For overlapping queues, inspect distinct task membership rather than summing totals as project usage. Expected result: an observed account of configured execution and reported usage. For missing telemetry, retain the unknown/partial label and inspect the source transcript; do not invent a token or billing estimate. Task rows and queue cards display reported token totals with session coverage. Task details and queue details include stages, configured provider/model pairs, session history, model switches and budget history. These are lifetime task totals through the current stage, including repair and review retries. Quota failures and automatic provider/model replacements are retained in the same session timeline and quota failover history. Their consumed sessions and reported tokens remain in totals even when a backup finishes the task. The execution ledger at .trust/manager/execution-ledger.jsonl records a stable session id at start and an updated record at exit. The latest record for that id wins: start, completion and repeated ingestion cannot double-count a session. Provider/model fields describe the actual launch configuration; a provider's internal routing or undisclosed model substitution cannot be inferred. Token collection accepts recognized CLI summaries and structured turn/result usage events. Structured turn events are summed within a process; cached input is included in input, not added a second time to the total. A plain tokens used summary supplies only the reported total. Unsupported or missing usage remains null. The UI shows partial totals and the number of sessions with unknown usage; an active or interrupted session without final telemetry is not zero tokens. These are CLI-reported observations, not provider billing verification. No price, token estimate, remote quota or model capability is guessed. Existing overnight session summaries are read without changing task state. Where no stored token field exists, the final 256 KiB of the transcript is inspected for a CLI usage summary. Old records cannot reliably reconstruct individual multi-turn structured events, missing sessions or missing budget decisions. They remain visibly partial. Raw prompts and transcripts are not copied into the execution ledger or learning memory. A queue report sums the lifetime reports of its distinct current member tasks. It also includes shared model planning, regeneration and plan review sessions matched by draft id, once per queue. Shared planning is not arbitrarily charged to each task. Queues with overlapping task membership are separate views; adding their totals together is not a project-wide spending total.

title: Execution reports
heading: Project memory and adaptation
text: Project memory and adaptation After a worker session, an immutable source snapshot of the task and its queue reports is archived in the existing project brain. Evidence-linked claims make the observations available in Knowledge. Planning sessions publish their own source snapshots. Repeated ingestion of an unchanged report is idempotent. The bounded learning memory is .trust/manager/resource-learning.json . Only done tasks with a current, non-invalidated independent review and an observed successful Beacon completion enter the calibration cohort. Failed or timed-out sessions do not become success samples. Samples retain the task, packet revision, complexity, risk, observed session count, review rejection count and immutable source revision. Legacy records without a recorded effort classification remain reportable but do not train resource decisions. For the same observed complexity and risk, at least three other completed tasks are required to replace the default initial estimate with the observed 75th percentile session count (minimum three sessions). Two completed tasks that required review repairs raise the required model tier by one. Both effects are shown in decision reasons. History is bounded to the latest thirty comparable tasks, from a retained set of five hundred. A task cannot train its own retry. This updates runtime estimates and selection rules through project evidence; it does not retrain model weights or rewrite ATL source code. Model allowlists, owner-controlled budgets, explicit run caps, workspace/browser permissions and independent verification gates still apply. Disabling automatic resources disables use of the calibration. Removing the resource-learning file resets calibration while preserving the original execution ledger and brain sources. Checks: node verification/execution_report_test.mjs , node verification/resource_policy_launch_test.mjs , node verification/execution_report_ui_test.mjs .

title: Jev routing
heading: How Jev saves context and tokens
text: How Jev saves context and tokens Jev is deliberately not another skill stack: - normal intake and normal routing make zero Jev calls; - --smart makes one request only; - the request contains the title, objective, labels, and route descriptions—not the repository or skill bodies; - the request asks one typed Choice , not for a generated explanation; - ATL does not retry through another model when Jev is unavailable; - low confidence and all transport failures use the existing deterministic router; - ATL adds no TypeSafe SDK dependency to the package. Jev can reduce wasted routing context. It does not reduce the tokens required by the worker to understand and implement a large task.

text: Trust boundary Jev is advisory. ATL remains authoritative for: - scope and user intent; - skill availability; - actor permissions; - status transitions; - evidence requirements; - review, merge, deployment, and destructive actions. A high-confidence Jev choice is routing evidence, not completion proof. The selected worker must still plan, implement, review, verify, and return the ATL Trust Verdict.

text: Interpret the result Term Meaning How to inspect it --- --- --- Objective Bounded intended outcome Read the task packet Completion check Observable acceptance condition Run its verifier and retain output Evidence Recorded observation tied to an artifact/revision Inspect task evidence and source Independent review A separate judgment on current changes Read findings and revision binding Blocker A condition that prevents permitted progress Read diagnostics and recovery Done Lifecycle completion under current runtime checks Inspect current evidence, not just the badge Delivery A concrete output boundary Distinguish local branch, PR, merge, deployment Trust Scoped autonomy justified by evidence Review task class and evidence history Process dose Smallest sufficient engineering route Use $atl and inspect routing reasons

An untrustworthy result lacks required evidence or violates its scope. These are review judgments, not substitutes for the literal runtime state contract.

title: Local API reference
heading: Owner-session boundary
text: Owner-session boundary The browser server binds to loopback by default. Browser-origin mutations use same-origin and owner-session/CSRF checks. Origin-less command-line requests remain supported by the outer guard; inspect each route rather than assuming universal session authentication. Some sensitive read operations, including change review, also require the owner cookie and x-atl-csrf header. A copied URL alone is insufficient authority. The browser client demonstrates the supported request flow. Read runtime/lib/session-auth.mjs , route guards in control-plane-server.mjs , and verification/owner_session_approval_test.mjs before integrating. Keep tokens out of logs and URLs.

title: Development and verification
heading: Set up
text: Set up Use Node.js 22+, Git, and Python for policy/formal checks. Browser tests need the project’s Playwright browser: npx playwright install chromium downloads it into the development environment.

title: Development and verification
heading: Choose meaningful checks
text: Choose meaningful checks Use the [feature map](guides.md) to find the implementing source and verifier. Most feature checks are standalone Node programs under verification/ . Read their setup before invoking them; a test name alone does not establish isolation. For the wider offline exercise, run node verification/run_mock_regression.mjs . See [verification README](../verification/README.md) for formal checks and the [recorded mock run](mock-system-e2e-2026-10-29.md) for evidence and limits.

title: Development and verification
heading: Record evidence
text: Record evidence Record command, revision/dirty overlay, exit code, output, fixture scope, failures, remedies, and final result. Fixture worker success demonstrates orchestration; real provider behavior needs separate evidence. Never record credentials.

title: Development and verification
heading: Validate documentation and package
text: Validate documentation and package Inspect runtime, skills, docs, license, and accidental private state in the package listing. Local checks do not publish a package or deploy Pages. Their configured GitHub workflows perform those actions after authorized triggers.

title: Development and verification
heading: Contribute
text: Contribute Follow source contracts and migrations, add meaningful behavior checks, and update the corresponding guide. Explain resulting behavior, validation, and remaining risks in review. Use [documentation workflow](documentation.md) for docs changes.

text: Documentation workflow Markdown is the editable source for public guides. A generator produces the GitHub Pages HTML and section search index. The package also includes the guides for local reading.

text: Find the source Resource Edit or inspect --- --- Guide text .md source in docs/site.json Navigation and titles docs/site.json HTML rendering scripts/build-docs.mjs Style and interaction docs/scss/styles.scss , docs/site.js Mermaid Fenced blocks in each guide Current screenshots docs/assets/screenshots/ Verification boundary docs/sync.yml , [refresh record](docs-refresh-verification.md) Historical evidence Existing dated reports/planning records Do not hand-edit generated top-level HTML, search-index.json , or vendor/mermaid.min.js . title: Documentation workflow
heading: Add or change a guide
text: Add or change a guide 1. Identify one reader goal and implementing source. 2. Add prerequisites, steps, expected results, and recovery. 3. Use relative Markdown links inside the repository. 4. Add public pages to docs/site.json . 5. Build, check, and inspect desktop/mobile rendering and search. 6. Advance the sync anchor only for checks that ran. Open the printed localhost URL. Search needs HTTP; file: browsing can prevent loading its index. Stop preview with Ctrl+C.

title: Documentation workflow
heading: Maintain diagrams and captures
text: Maintain diagrams and captures Keep a diagram focused on one question and explain its relationships in prose. Mermaid uses a local pinned bundle with strict settings. Label conceptual models separately from literal fields. See [diagram library](diagrams.md). Run node scripts/docs-preview.mjs for an isolated, read-only synthetic Control Plane. Navigate and capture actual rendered screens. Record date, fixture, viewport, and limitations. Keep production task data and provider secrets out of captures.

title: Documentation workflow
heading: Verify and publish
text: Verify and publish npm run docs:check checks generated freshness, source links, HTML links/anchors, search coverage, assets, and catalog consistency. Browser review separately checks rendered diagrams, search, theme, and responsive navigation. Run npm run docs:test for the offline browser regression. It checks every public page and exercises search, empty results, keyboard focus, code copying, persistent theme, mobile navigation, and ER diagrams. External network requests are blocked. Its evidence is written to .atl-evidence/docs-refresh/ and retained by the documentation CI workflow. Pages builds and checks before uploading docs/ . Package publication checks docs first. Local build/check commands do not publish remotely. Confirm GitHub workflow results after an authorized push or release.

title: Documentation verification
heading: Coverage and organization
text: Coverage and organization The site has 37 public pages , with Markdown sources registered in docs/site.json . Every public guide is searchable. The resource model includes core work and trust/learning ER diagrams, task and queue fields, persistent file ownership, and a task-tracing procedure. The generated file catalog inventories maintained source families and explains their purposes. Coverage includes installation, Control Plane menus, Jira/GitHub/Azure intake, description-to-plan review, task contracts, queues, overnight execution, recovery, Ask ATL, change review, model routing, budgets, access, quota fallback, execution reports, learning, research, source maps, projects, approvals, backups, routines, and history transport. CLI, console, lifecycle, skill, and API route references are generated from their source contracts. Seven current Control Plane screenshots show Overview, Tasks, Issue sources, Plan Studio, Queues, Agent Team, and Ask ATL. They use an isolated read-only synthetic project. [Screenshot provenance](assets/screenshots/README.md) and assets/screenshots/captures.json record their source, dimensions, and hashes. No production issue was fetched and no provider session was launched for captures. Executable skills, command contracts, research decisions, and dated evidence are cataloged rather than rewritten into simplified instructions that could change their meaning. Existing public HTML routes remain stable. Historical reports retain their actual failures and dates.
